slides.title: US entry in 2027: go in through Amazon, and earn the way into specialty retail

paragraphs.text: US entry in 2027: go in through Amazon, and earn the way into specialty retail
Should Onsoo enter the US market in 2027, and if so, by which route? Recommendation for CEO Park Ji-won and the board, March 2027 board meeting
Prepared November 2026 from the planning-team briefing pack only (no outside research).
All company, competitor and market figures in the pack are synthetic benchmark data.

slides.notes: Deck built only from evidence/briefing-pack.md. Judgment calls made without client input are listed in the appendix.

slides.title: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon. Do not launch 600 retail doors, and hold the Japan scale-up for a later year

paragraphs.text: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon. Do not launch 600 retail doors, and hold the Japan scale-up for a later year

Recommendation: approve Option A (Amazon-led) for 2027 with a $4M US cash envelope. Reject Option B (600-door retail launch) and defer Option J (Japan scale-up). Add specialty retail only once aided awareness passes 20%.
Only Amazon-led fits the board’s limits
What the board has to accept
US K-beauty skincare reached $3.6B in 2025, growing 17% a year against 5% for all facial skincare
41% of it sells on Amazon, and 61% of K-beauty buyers buy there most often
The pilot works: monthly units +89% in six months, 4.5 stars, repeat close to benchmark (29% vs 31%)
Retail-led breaks the $18M cap (−$20.8M peak), never pays back and pulls group margin to 4.5%, even on its own inputs
Those inputs are optimistic: brands at Onsoo’s awareness sell 2.6 units/door/week; the retailer removes brands below 4.0
Amazon-led needs $1.9–3.9M of peak cash and keeps group margin at 9% or more
Payback by 2030 holds only if ACoS stays at or below 28.6%. At the 32% scaling benchmark it slips to about 2032
No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the limits. Option A reaches ~$26M; reset $40M as a 2031–32 milestone
Guardrails on ad cost, cash and repeat purchase bring the decision back to the board early
Source: briefing pack (Tables 1–9, survey Sep 2026); team model of planning-team inputs. ACoS = Amazon ad spend as a share of Amazon sales.

slides.notes: Answer first. Everything after this slide supports one of the three columns.

slides.title: Only the Amazon-led route fits within the board’s limits. The retail-led route breaks three of them on its own numbers

paragraphs.text: THE DECISION AGAINST THE BOARD’S TESTS
Only the Amazon-led route fits within the board’s limits. The retail-led route breaks three of them on its own numbers
US business “on the way to $40M by 2030”
$26.4M US revenue in 2030, still growing ~30% a year
$37.6M in 2030 on paper, but only by breaking three limits
No US business. Adds $7.0M of Japan revenue by 2030
Cumulative cash back to zero by end-2030
−$20.8M at end-2030. Operating loss every year

Uses the 2027 slot. The US waits

Note: planning-team inputs unless stated. “32% ACoS” = agency median for brands scaling $5M→$20M on Amazon US. (1) J excludes working capital (not given). Source: briefing pack Tables 4–7; team model.

slides.title: The US prize is K-beauty skincare: $3.6B in 2025 and growing about 17% a year, more than three times as fast as the category

paragraphs.text: The US prize is K-beauty skincare: $3.6B in 2025 and growing about 17% a year, more than three times as fast as the category
K-beauty skincare sales in 2025: 14.7% of a $24.5B category, up from 9.5% in 2021
K-beauty growth 2021–25, against 5% for the category and 3.5% for all other brands
Share of 2025 K-beauty skincare sales that the $40M ambition represents
Not comparable: the trade-press “$5.2B US K-beauty market” includes makeup and hair care. We use the $3.6B skincare figure throughout.
Source: briefing pack Table 1 (US facial skincare sales, $B); trade-press article (2026). Growth = compound annual rate 2021–25.

slides.title: US K-beauty buyers shop and discover online. Amazon and TikTok, not the store, are where a new brand gets found

paragraphs.text: US K-beauty buyers shop and discover online. Amazon and TikTok, not the store, are where a new brand gets found
Share of US K-beauty skincare sales, 2025
K-beauty buyers: where they buy most often
K-beauty buyers: where they found their last new brand

Implication: build awareness where buyers already are: Amazon for purchase, TikTok and influencers for discovery. Price matters too: 52% of K-beauty triers name “price compared with US brands” as a reason, which favours the $24 Amazon price over a $28 shelf price.
Source: briefing pack Table 2 (channel shares of US K-beauty skincare sales, 2025); survey of 1,200 US women 18–44, Sep 2026 (K-beauty buyer sub-sample).

slides.title: The Amazon pilot shows growing demand: monthly units nearly doubled in six months at 4.5 stars

paragraphs.text: The Amazon pilot shows growing demand: monthly units nearly doubled in six months at 4.5 stars
Ad cost of sales (ACoS) over the pilot, on a small budget
90-day repeat. First-year US benchmark 31%; Onsoo Korea 48%
of reviews flag Korean-only labels. US labels are in the setup budget
Pilot sales: 64,800 units, about $1.56M at the $24 selling price.
2027 plan needs more: 300k units = 25k a month, 1.8× the June run-rate. It relies on four new SKUs, and monthly growth slowed from 16–17% (Feb–Apr) to 8–9% (May–Jun).
Source: briefing pack section 6 (Amazon pilot Jan–Jun 2026, three SKUs, cross-border seller); Table 5 (2027 forecast).

slides.title: An Amazon unit earns $4.73 at the planned 25% ad cost but only $3.05 at the 32% benchmark. Retail earns more per unit but carries far more fixed cost

paragraphs.text: An Amazon unit earns $4.73 at the planned 25% ad cost but only $3.05 at the 32% benchmark. Retail earns more per unit but carries far more fixed cost
Option B adds $7.5M a year of fixed cost: national marketing $6.0M and field sales $1.5M
Covering it at $7.55 a unit takes ~994k retail units a year: about 4,250 doors at 4.5 units/door/week
The plan has 600 doors in 2027, selling 140k units
Ads are the largest controllable Amazon cost: each point of ACoS = $0.24 a unit
At 32% ACoS, ads cost $7.68 and contribution falls to $3.05 (−36%).
Source: briefing pack Table 4 (Rice Ferment Barrier Cream, per unit, applied to all SKUs as the planning team does), Table 6; agency ACoS benchmark (section 11).

slides.title: Even on the planning team’s inputs, the retail-led route breaks the $18M cap, never pays back and takes group margin below 8% for three years

paragraphs.text: OPTION B ON ITS OWN NUMBERS
Even on the planning team’s inputs, the retail-led route breaks the $18M cap, never pays back and takes group margin below 8% for three years
Cumulative US (or Japan) cash flow from launch, $M
Why the numbers do not work
Versus A, B adds $7.5M a year of fixed cost plus $1.2M of launch fee and fixtures
In return its retail leg earns $1.1–1.8M a year and the assumed Amazon halo $0.4–1.6M
Net: B’s operating profit is $4.4–7.2M a year below A’s in every year to 2030
Source: team model of planning-team inputs (Tables 4–7): 25% ACoS, 4.5 units/door/week, 1.3× Amazon halo; inventory = 4 months of landed cost. J excludes working capital.

slides.title: And B’s inputs are optimistic: at Onsoo’s awareness, newcomer brands sell about 2.6 units per door a week, well below the 4.0 the retailer requires

paragraphs.text: And B’s inputs are optimistic: at Onsoo’s awareness, newcomer brands sell about 2.6 units per door a week, well below the 4.0 the retailer requires
First-year units per door per week, by brand awareness
It comes from the retailer’s deck on successful newcomers. Even the top quartile of brands at <10% awareness (3.4) falls short of 4.0, so Onsoo would likely be removed after its first year.
The 0.71 link between doors and Amazon sales can run the other way: retailers add brands that already sell. Saebom built ~$30M on Amazon first, then added 300 doors in 2025.
Retailer removes brands below 4.0 after 12 months
Retail-first in 450 doors in 2023, removed from shelves in 2025, est. $21M US loss, more than Onsoo’s whole $18M cap.
With 2.6 units, no halo and 32% ACoS, B’s cumulative cash reaches −$31M by 2030, even if it is never removed from shelves.
Bars = median; whiskers = interquartile range. Awareness = aided, among category buyers.

Source: briefing pack Table 8 (retail analytics firm, 2025, 46 brands); survey Sep 2026; Table 9; board-member memo. Awareness measured among category buyers (all facial-skincare buyers), the base Table 8 uses.

slides.title: Option A pays back by 2030 only if ad cost stays at or below 28.6% of sales. Above that, payback slips, but the cash at risk stays small

paragraphs.text: Option A pays back by 2030 only if ad cost stays at or below 28.6% of sales. Above that, payback slips, but the cash at risk stays small
Option A cumulative cash flow by ad cost (ACoS), $M
Blue = pays back by 2030. Red = does not.
Break-even ACoS is 28.6%, or 26.9% if the duty rises to 25%. The pilot ran at 28%
The plan assumes ACoS falls to 25%; the benchmark says it rises with scale as click costs climb
In every case peak cash stays ≤ $7.5M and group margin ≥ 8.7%
Source: team model; pilot ACoS 28% (section 6); agency benchmark: median ACoS 32% (range 26–38%) for brands scaling $5M→$20M on Amazon US (section 11); tariff review (section 13).

slides.title: If Amazon stalls the way it did for two peers, Option A loses about $7M. A retail-first failure costs three times that

paragraphs.text: If Amazon stalls the way it did for two peers, Option A loses about $7M. A retail-first failure costs three times that
Amazon-first does not guarantee scale: two of three peers stayed below $5M. But that failure is cheap and shows early, so it can be stopped. The retail-first failure cost more than Onsoo’s whole cap.
B realistic = 2.6 units/door/week, no halo, 32% ACoS.
Source: team model; briefing pack Table 9 (public reporting and interviews). Stall case: 200k units a year (~$4.8M revenue, like Gaon Lab and Yeoreum) at 32% ACoS, fixed costs unchanged.

slides.title: The Japan scale-up is safe but small: $7M of added revenue by 2030, in a market growing 1.5% a year, and it leaves the US untouched

paragraphs.text: The Japan scale-up is safe but small: $7M of added revenue by 2030, in a market growing 1.5% a year, and it leaves the US untouched

If ACoS runs at 32%, J returns more cash by 2030. But it adds only $7M of revenue and does nothing for the US ambition. A builds a $26M business still growing ~30% a year. Keep J on the list for 2028 or later, once the US team is running.
Source: briefing pack Table 7, group context, section 8; team model. J excludes working capital (not given). Growth rates: K-beauty US 2021–25 CAGR; Japan facial skincare per pack.

slides.title: No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the board’s limits. Keep the limits and move the $40M milestone to about 2032

paragraphs.text: No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the board’s limits. Keep the limits and move the $40M milestone to about 2032
Only B gets close ($37.6M), and only by breaking the cash cap, the payback test and the margin floor, on inputs that look optimistic.
Keep the limits, move the date
A reaches ~$26M in 2030. At +25% a year it passes $40M around 2032, sooner if the retail gates (next page) are met.
Source: team model of Table 5 volumes. 2031–32 is an illustrative extension at +25% a year (below the plan’s +29% in 2030); it is not a planning-team forecast.

slides.title: Add retail later, through tighter gates: awareness above 20% (not 15%) and a first step the group margin can absorb

paragraphs.text: Add retail later, through tighter gates: awareness above 20% (not 15%) and a first step the group margin can absorb
20% or more aided awareness among all facial-skincare buyers (today 4%)
At 10–20% awareness newcomers sell a median 3.5 units/door/week (IQR 2.8–4.3): most fall below the 4.0 removal bar. Above 20% the median is 4.6.
$20M or more a year at ACoS of 30% or less
Retail’s fixed costs need a profitable base. Saebom reached ~$30M before adding doors. On plan, A reaches $20M in 2029.
Not specified (board member proposes 600 doors nationally)
A test of ~300 doors, with a budget below the margin headroom
In 2030, group profit above the 8% floor is only $3.9–5.7M. B’s retail leg costs $4.4–7.2M a year more than A.
When the gates are met, which means planning for 2030 at the earliest
Awareness has to rise five-fold from 4%. Track it every six months from the 2027 launch.
Source: briefing pack Table 8, Table 9, section 4 (CEO hypothesis), survey Sep 2026; team model (2030 headroom = group operating profit above 8% of revenue with Option A at 32% / 25% ACoS).

slides.title: Approve the Amazon-led launch with a $4M cash envelope and guardrails that bring the decision back to the board early

paragraphs.text: Approve the Amazon-led launch with a $4M cash envelope and guardrails that bring the decision back to the board early
Enter the US in 2027 via the Amazon-led route. No 600-door retail launch; no Japan scale-up in 2027
Above 32% for two quarters in a row
Authorise up to $4M of cumulative US cash outflow. Any need beyond that returns to the board
Accept that 2030 payback is at risk. On plan if ACoS ≤ 28.6%; at 32% ACoS, about 2032
Reset the ambition: $40M as a 2031–32 milestone; add retail only through the gates on page 14
Still ≤ 29% after US labels and new SKUs
Rises to 25% (mid-2027 decision): re-plan, break-even ACoS 26.9%
Surveyed every six months; feeds the retail gate

First moves in 2027: set up the US entity and MoCRA registration · US-English labels (fixes the 6% complaint) · take the listings over from the cross-border seller · launch four new SKUs · hire the US team · first awareness survey in Q3

Source: team analysis. The $4M envelope covers the 32% ACoS + 25% duty case (peak −$3.9M). The unit trigger matches the stall case on page 11. 2032 payback at 32% ACoS uses the illustrative +25%/yr extension (page 13).

slides.title: How the options were modelled: the planning team’s inputs, applied consistently, with benchmark cases added

paragraphs.text: How the options were modelled: the planning team’s inputs, applied consistently, with benchmark cases added
Per-unit contribution (hero product, applied to all SKUs as the planning team does)
Amazon: $24.00 − 15% referral − $5.10 FBA − $3.50 product − $0.55 freight − 15% duty on product − ACoS × price = $4.73 at 25% ACoS
Retail: $14.00 wholesale − $3.50 − $0.75 freight − $0.53 duty − 8% co-op − 4% returns = $7.55
Retail volume = doors × 4.5 units × 52 weeks; B Amazon units = A × 1.3
Fixed and one-time costs per Table 6; fixtures $1,100 for each new door in the year it opens
Inventory held = 4 months of that year’s landed cost (product + freight + duty); cash flow = operating profit − increase in inventory
Option J: revenue × 30% − $0.8M a year − $1.0M one-time; no working capital given, so none included
Peak cash = lowest cumulative cash flow, 2027–30
Group margin = (ex-US plan revenue × 11% + option operating profit) ÷ (ex-US revenue + option revenue)
Benchmark: 32% ACoS, the agency median for $5M→$20M brands; range 26–38% tested
Tariff: duty 25% on product cost, applied to all four years (a conservative stress)
Not modelled: FX (a weaker won would help), tax, cost inflation, post-2030 terminal value
Source: briefing pack sections 6–8 and 13. All figures are synthetic benchmark data.
